html:
A poet of the Tang dynasty in China, famous for poems about wine, the moon, mountains and the free life of a wanderer. He is still one of the most read and loved poets in Chinese.

He grew up in Sichuan and spent much of his life on the road. For a short time, in the 740s, he served at the court of Emperor Xuanzong in Chang'an, but he left or was sent away. In 744 he met the younger poet Du Fu, who wrote poems to him for years after.

When the An Lushan Rebellion broke out, he joined the staff of a prince who was later branded a rebel. He was sentenced to exile but pardoned on the way.

His poems seem easy and spontaneous, and they use the plain forms of folk song as well as strict verse. "Quiet Night Thought", about moonlight on the floor and thoughts of home, is learned by children across China. A legend says he drowned trying to embrace the moon in a river.
